Lines.Text: CREEEAK— BANG.
The heavy door groaned open. All five girls, sprawled on the floor and struggling for breath, turned toward it.
P stood in the doorway.
(her eyes widening as she scrambles up) P...? Oh my God, your face! What happened?!
The girls rushed to him in horror. He was a wreck.
His once-neat jacket was caked in dirt and mud.
His trousers were badly torn at the knees, the fabric crusted with blood.
The soles of his old shoes had worn almost clean off and hung loose.
(close to tears) You're bleeding... What did they do to you out there...?
(her lips trembling with anger) S-Tier did this, didn't they? Did someone lay a hand on you?! I'm calling the pol—
No. We won.
They went still.
With his legs trembling, P steadied himself against the wall, then reached inside his jacket and pulled out a crumpled bundle of paper.
Dirt and small bloodstains marked it.
He unfolded it as carefully as if it were the most precious jewel in the world, and held it out to them.
[ M-Beat Live Broadcast Cue Sheet ] [ Stage - Rookie Girl Group (V.E.L.O.) ]
Next Thursday. M-Beat Live. Three minutes, thirty seconds.
(catching her breath) M-Beat... Live? That's a prime-time live broad—
I spent three days begging everyone from the station director to the most junior producer.
Wore my knees raw. Finally, they threw me a slot someone had dropped out of.
Then I worked construction on their sets to earn it.
His voice began to thicken.
You're making your debut.
At those words, the tension holding the girls upright snapped.
Aaaaagh...!
Hana was the first to collapse. The girl who always hid behind Jiwoo, watching everyone for permission, sank to the floor sobbing.
Jiwoo wrapped her arms around her and began to cry aloud.
Even Seoyun covered her face with both hands, her shoulders shaking. Ria clung to P's clothes and cried like a child.
(taking the running order with shaking hands) This... This is real, right...? We're really going to stand in front of those cameras...?
(nodding, kneeling to meet their eyes) Listen to me. This basement goes to auction next month. This performance is the last bomb we've got left to throw at the world.
Our... last...?
It's live, nationwide. Ten percent of the audience share. Millions of people watching us in real time.
S-Tier can yank our leash all they want, but once the red light goes on, there's nothing they can do.
No edits. No control. Just one shot. Three minutes, thirty seconds.
Now they understood why P had fought until he was bloody for this one live performance.
Something fiercer than gratitude began to kindle in their eyes.
Give them a performance so perfect they forget how to breathe. Make them remember you in those three and a half minutes.
Once they do... not even someone bigger than S-Tier can erase us.
(clenching her fists) You crawled through the dirt to get us on that broadcast. We'll eat those cameras alive. Make sure nobody forgets us.
(getting up, roughly wiping tears from the tops of her feet) I want those S-Tier executives watching live when their knees give out.
On the basement floor, the five girls and their mud-covered producer held one another, sharing the warmth of a miracle.
From that day on, the basement became a battlefield where they pushed themselves past every limit.
Four in the morning. Over the crackle of cheap speakers, their ragged breathing mingled with the smell of blood.
Thud, thud—BANG!!
Hey! Your center of gravity came up on that crossover!
Got it! Watch me—I can fly with my feet glued to the floor!
Ria, when you punch through with that vocal, sing like you're trying to shatter the TV!
I know! (coughing) My throat can bleed all it wants. I won't go flat. Don't worry!
The girls forgot how to sleep. Their bodies were gaunt, running on a single cup of noodles a day, but—

They survived on a single cup of instant noodles each day, their bodies growing gaunt. Yet the choreography they meant to sear into millions of minds was savage, precise, and powerful enough to seem to break their bones.
Seoyun's scraped knees bled through her white practice clothes.
Mina's big toenail, battered by her relentless pursuit of a perfect turn, blackened and finally fell off.
She did not scream. With shaking hands, she bound her injured bare foot in duct tape and returned to the mirror.
Even Hana, who always hid behind someone else, bit down on her bleeding lip, stared into an imagined main camera in the mirror, and spat out her rap with venom.
One live broadcast. Three minutes, thirty seconds that nobody could edit away.
Everything they had lived for rested on that fleeting stage.
They willingly fed it their flesh, their bones, and every last piece of their souls.
